slug.description: The domain with dots replaced by hyphens. Unique, so a-b.com and a.b.com collide.

Must contain a dot and match `^(?:[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?\.)+[a-z]{2,}$`. Flyn domains and well-known public platforms are refused. A non-string value returns 500.

routing.description: A @ 76.76.21.21 when the custom domain is the registrable domain itself (for example example.com or example.com.br), otherwise a CNAME to cname.flyn.to whose name is the subdomain part.

message.description: Next step, for example "Domain is verified and active!".

verified.description: True only when the TXT record matches, routing is configured and hosting ownership is confirmed.

category.description: Why a destination was blocked (DESTINATION_BLOCKED only), for example `malware`.

domain.description: Short domain the link lives on. New links default to the current Flyn short domain.

password.description: True when the link is password protected. The password itself is never returned.

targeting.description: Smart-routing rules, or null when there are none.

destinationUrl.description: The stored destination the visitor was sent to (the fallback URL once a click limit is reached), before query-string passthrough.

variant.description: The destination id when a rotation chose the destination. timestamp.description: Unix time in milliseconds; the same value as t= in X-Flyn-Signature.

abSplit.description: **Pro.** Legacy A/B split, percent kept on the primary url. Clamped to 0..100; a non-finite value becomes 50.

abUrlB.description: **Pro.** Legacy A/B variant URL. http or https, not a Flyn host (400 "Cannot shorten Flyn URLs"), public IP, safety scanned (422).

clickLimit.description: **Pro.** Maximum human clicks. null or "" is ignored.

deepLink.description: **Pro.** Serve the native-app handoff page on mobile. null returns 400.

domain.description: Short domain. Default: the current Flyn short domain; the legacy value `www.flyn.to` is treated as a request for that default. Any other value must exactly match (case-sensitive) a custom domain owned by the workspace, else 403. **Pro** for any custom domain.

expiresAt.description: Expiry (ISO 8601). Must parse as a date; past dates are accepted and stored as sent.

fallbackUrl.description: **Pro.** Destination once the click limit is reached. `https://` is prepended; http or https, not a Flyn host, public IP, safety scanned (422).

forwardParams.description: Pass the short link's query string through to the destination.

noIndex.description: **Pro** when true. Accepted and stored for compatibility. It has no effect on how the link is served: every short link is already served with a noindex robots header on every plan, whether or not this is set.

ogImage.description: Social preview image. http or https; the host must resolve to a public IP.

password.description: **Pro.** Password gate (stored as a bcrypt hash). An empty string is ignored.

pixelIds.description: **Pro.** Saved pixel ids to fire. Ids outside the workspace are dropped silently. If any id is not a valid UUID, every id is dropped (no error).

rotation.description: **Pro.** Weighted rotation across up to 12 destinations (more returns 400). Each destination must be http or https, must not be a Flyn host (400 "Cannot shorten Flyn URLs"), must not resolve to a private address (400), and is safety scanned (422).

slug.description: Custom back-half. Not a reserved word (case-insensitive). Default: 6 random characters. Unique per domain (409 on clash).

targeting.description: **Pro.** Strict shape `{device?: {ios?, android?, windows?, macos?}, geo?: {<ISO alpha-2>: url}}`. Any other key, a non-object, a non-string value or a geo key that is not two letters returns 400 `INVALID_TARGETING`, and so do the device aliases `mac`, `osx`, `win`, `desktop` and `linux`, with a hint in the message. There is no desktop key: Linux, ChromeOS and other systems fall through to the link's other rules. Country codes are upper-cased, values trimmed, empty parts dropped. `windows` and `macos` must be http or https URLs (400 `INVALID_TARGETING` otherwise); `ios`, `android` and `geo` values are not validated as URLs. Values are safety scanned (422), and a value on a Flyn host returns 400 "Cannot shorten Flyn URLs". A `macos` rule adds the Safari check page described on Targeting.

title.description: Display title. Default: the part of the URL after `//` up to the next `/` (usually the hostname, but it keeps any port or userinfo, and a query or fragment when there is no path), else "Untitled".

url.description: Destination. Trimmed; `https://` is prepended unless it starts with http:, https:, mailto:, tel:, sms: or ftp:. ftp: is always refused. For http(s): the host must contain a dot, must not be a Flyn host, and must resolve in DNS to a public IP (else 400 "Private/internal URLs are not allowed"). mailto:, tel: and sms: skip host checks. Then a safety scan (422 when blocked); a deeper scan runs after the response and can disable the link later.

data.description: The link as it was before deletion.

shortUrl.description: The clean short URL. The image itself encodes this URL plus `?flyn_qr=1`, the scan marker behind `qrScans`.

svg.description: SVG markup; present only when format=svg.

data.description: The full updated Link for PATCH /api/links/{id}; the id plus the changed fields for dashboard edits.

Fields marked **Pro** return 403 `UPGRADE_REQUIRED` on a Free plan when set to a real value; false, [], null and "" pass that plan check so a downgraded account can switch features off, but null is refused (400) for domain, deepLink, forwardParams and pixelIds: send the default short domain, false or [] instead.

abSplit.description: **Pro** when non-zero. Clamped to 0..100; same 409 rule as abUrlB.

abUrlB.description: **Pro** when non-empty. Returns 409 `ROTATION_ACTIVE` when the link has a stored rotation other than the legacy two-destination A/B pair (ids A and B) and `rotation` is not sent in the same request; update `rotation` instead. Otherwise the create rules apply, including 400 "Cannot shorten Flyn URLs" for a Flyn host.

clickLimit.description: **Pro** when set. null or "" clears it.

conversionTracking.description: **Pro** when true. Stored as `value === true`, so any other value (including the string "true") turns tracking off.

deepLink.description: **Pro** when true. Send a JSON boolean; null returns 400.

domain.description: Moves the link to another short domain. The current Flyn short domain, or the legacy value `www.flyn.to`, moves it back to the default. A pending or paused domain is accepted, but the link does not serve until the domain is active. Sending the link's current domain changes nothing. **Pro** for a custom domain. null or an empty string returns 400.

expiresAt.description: Must parse as a date; null clears it.

fallbackUrl.description: **Pro** when set. null or "" clears it; otherwise the same rules as create.

folderId.description: Folder in the workspace (404 otherwise); null clears it. Moving a link into a different folder needs Pro or Lifetime (403 UPGRADE_REQUIRED on Free); on Free, set folderId when you create the link. Sending the link's current folder is always accepted.

noIndex.description: **Pro** when true. Accepted and stored for compatibility. It has no effect on how the link is served: every short link is already served with a noindex robots header on every plan, whether or not this is set.

password.description: **Pro** when non-empty. A non-empty string is hashed and set; null or "" removes the password.

pixelIds.description: **Pro** when non-empty. Ids outside the workspace are dropped; [] clears; null returns 400. If any id is not a valid UUID the list is set to [].

rotation.description: **Pro** when it normalises to a rotation. Replaces the whole list (existing ids kept, missing ids minted). Destinations follow the create rules, including 400 "Cannot shorten Flyn URLs" for a Flyn host.

slug.description: New back-half; not reserved; 409 on clash. null or an empty string returns 400.

status.description: Any other value returns 400, including an empty string or null.

targeting.description: **Pro** when it normalises to rules. Same strict shape and checks as create (400 `INVALID_TARGETING`). domain.description: Anonymous callers always get the anonymous short domain; this field is ignored. Authenticated callers default to the current Flyn short domain (the legacy value `www.flyn.to` is treated as a request for that default); any other value must be a custom domain owned in scope, else 403.

slug.description: Custom back-half, allowed for anonymous callers too. Default: 6 random characters. 409 on clash.

tags.description: Stored as sent for every caller. Default [].

url.description: Destination (raw length at most 2048). Scheme rules as POST /api/links. For http(s): the host needs a dot, must not be a Flyn host, passes a category blocklist (422), must resolve publicly (else 400 "Invalid URL"), then a safety scan (422).

authenticated.description: True when the link belongs to an account (API key or session).

expiresAt.description: Anonymous links expire 24 hours after creation; authenticated links have no expiry (null).

Targeting.description: Smart-routing rules as stored. `device` takes four keys, `ios`, `android`, `windows` and `macos`, each applying only to visitors on that operating system, and a device rule takes priority. There is no `desktop` key: Linux, ChromeOS and any other or unrecognised system match no device rule and fall through to the link's other rules. `windows` and `macos` must be http or https URLs, and the aliases `mac`, `osx`, `win`, `desktop` and `linux` are rejected with 400 `INVALID_TARGETING`. `geo` maps ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes (upper case) to a destination and applies to every visitor whose country is known, desktop included. A visitor matching no rule falls through to the rotation, or the legacy A/B split, when one is set, else goes to the link url. A PATCH replaces the whole targeting object; nothing is merged into the stored rules. Safari on an iPad usually sends the same user agent as Safari on a Mac, so on a link with a `macos` destination, Safari on a Mac or an iPad (or any browser sending that same user agent) first loads a blank check page that tells a Mac from an iPad, then continues at once. A browser with JavaScript off continues as a Mac. The check page records no click; the click is recorded once, when the browser continues to the short link with the reserved query parameters `flyn_os` and `flyn_ref` (the original referrer), which are never passed to a destination. Chrome, Edge and Firefox on a Mac skip the check page, and a link without a `macos` rule never shows it. Device and country rules, including the Safari check page, do not apply to password-protected links, to a link that has reached its click limit, or to mailto, tel and sms links.

ios.description: Destination for iOS visitors, such as an iPhone. Safari on an iPad usually sends the same user agent as Safari on a Mac (see Targeting).

macos.description: Destination for Mac visitors. Must be an http or https URL, for example a Mac App Store or download page. Setting it turns on the Safari check page described on Targeting.

windows.description: Destination for Windows visitors. Must be an http or https URL, for example a Microsoft Store or download page.

geo.description: Country code to destination, for example {"US": "https://example.com/us"}.

canEdit.description: GET /api/webhooks only. True when the caller may PATCH it: only its creator can, and for a team webhook the creator also needs a role in that team that may edit webhooks (owner, admin or member, not a viewer).

failureCount.description: Failures in a row since the last success or reactivation: non-2xx answers, timeouts, connection errors, refused redirects, and skips of a URL whose host resolves to a private address or fails DNS resolution. At 10 the webhook is set inactive and its creator is emailed.

isOwner.description: GET /api/webhooks only. True when the caller created this webhook; only the creator can delete it or send a test ping.

lastTriggeredAt.description: Unix time in milliseconds of the last successful delivery. Absent from the create response.

secret.description: Signing secret, `whsec_` + 48 hex. Always in full in the create response. Afterwards API-key callers see only a masked prefix (first 8 characters); the creator's own dashboard session sees it in full.

status.description: A webhook becomes inactive after 10 counted delivery failures in a row.

events.description: Events to subscribe to. Unknown names are dropped silently; 400 only when none remain. A non-array value returns 500.

url.description: Endpoint that receives deliveries. Trimmed; http or https; must not resolve to a private address. A non-string value returns 500.

error.description: Present when no answer came back (network error, DNS failure, 10 s timeout, redirect to a private host, too many redirects).

status.description: HTTP status your endpoint answered with.

statusText.description: Present when the endpoint answered non-2xx.

WebhookUpdateRequest.description: All fields optional. An empty body succeeds and changes nothing but the update time.

events.description: Replaces the subscription. Every name must be known, else 400 "Invalid events: ...".

url.description: http or https, not a private address.

OAuth access tokens issued to MCP clients (`Bearer flyn_mcp_at_...`, every plan) are accepted only by GET and POST /api/links, GET /api/links/{id}/clicks, GET /api/links/{id}/qr, POST /api/qr and POST /api/shorten; every other authenticated endpoint answers 401 to them (the conversion ingest endpoints need no authentication and ignore the header).

info.description:
The Flyn REST API creates and manages short links, QR codes, custom domains, retargeting pixels, conversion tracking and webhooks.

**Base URL:** `https://www.flyn.to`. Every path starts with `/api`. Request and response bodies are JSON.

**Authentication:** send `Authorization: Bearer flyn_sk_live_<64 hex>`. Create keys in Settings > API Keys (`/settings?tab=api`); creating a key requires a Pro, Lifetime or Team plan, where Team means a member of a paying owner's workspace (effective plan `team`), and in a team workspace a role other than viewer. A key acts with its creator's current role. Some endpoints also accept the signed-in dashboard session cookie, and six accept OAuth access tokens issued to AI assistants over MCP (`Bearer flyn_mcp_at_...`, available on every plan). Each operation says which it accepts. The conversion ingest endpoints need no authentication.

**Workspace:** a key acts in its own team, or else in the workspace the user last selected in the dashboard, as long as that membership is still active.

**Plan rules:** paid features answer 403 with `code: UPGRADE_REQUIRED` and `upgradeUrl: /pricing` on the Free plan. A key keeps working if its account later moves to Free, and the Free limits described on each operation then apply. Team members inherit the plan of a paying, non-suspended workspace owner.

**Rate limits:** every limit is counted per client IP address, not per key or account. Each endpoint has its own fixed window that starts at the first request and is held in memory on each server instance, except where operations share a bucket: POST and PATCH /api/pixels share one, the GET and POST ingest operations on /api/conversion and /api/postback share one, POST /api/domains/add shares one with its alias POST /api/domains, and DELETE /api/domains/{id} shares one with DELETE /api/domains/{id}/delete, the route the dashboard's trash icon calls. Limits are checked before authentication unless an operation says otherwise. A 429 carries `Retry-After` (seconds) unless the operation says it does not.

**Errors:** `{"error": "<message>"}`, sometimes with `code` (UPGRADE_REQUIRED, DESTINATION_BLOCKED, INVALID_TARGETING, ROTATION_ACTIVE, LIMIT_REACHED, DAILY_LIMIT, MONTHLY_LIMIT, ROLE_FORBIDDEN) and extra fields such as `upgradeUrl`, `limit`, `used`, `premiumFields`, `category` or `signupUrl`. The conversion ingest endpoints answer `{"ok": false, "error": "<message>"}` instead.

**Webhooks:** Flyn signs every delivery with HMAC-SHA256; see the webhooks section for payloads and signature verification.

**Short links:** examples show short URLs on flyn.co, the domain new links are created on by default.

Guides and examples: https://www.flyn.to/docs

post.description:
Sent for each human click (bots are filtered out) to the webhooks of the user who created the link. Also sent when a password-protected link is unlocked (that path does not filter bots) and for mailto:, tel: and sms: links. The payload has no os or browser field.

Every delivery is an HTTP POST with a JSON body `{event, timestamp, data}`. `X-Flyn-Signature` is `t=<timestamp>,v1=<hex>`, where v1 is HMAC-SHA256 keyed with the full webhook secret (including the `whsec_` prefix) over `<t>.<raw request body>`. To verify: split the header on commas, recompute the HMAC over t, a dot and the raw body bytes (not a re-serialised body), compare in constant time, and reject a t (milliseconds) older than your tolerance. Flyn makes one delivery attempt per event with a 10 s timeout (redirects included). A 2xx answer counts as success; a non-2xx answer counts as a failure, and after 10 counted failures in a row the webhook is set inactive. A URL whose host resolves to a private address or fails DNS resolution is not sent to and counts as a failure. Timeouts, connection errors and redirects to a private host are not counted.
